description: Harden the shipped wallet-verification flow by introducing Decimal-safe BTC arithmetic, real gap-limit-based discovery semantics, explicit confirmed-versus-unconfirmed verification policy, and verification-path performance and contract cleanup so the wallet and dashboard Verified posture remains trustworthy as operator usage grows.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed after Feature-23 merge so hardening work can target the shipped wallet and dashboard verification surfaces directly.

principles: Keep the Core-plus-Electrum verification architecture intact
Prefer correctness and operator trust over new convenience features
Implement the scan semantics that the UI and PRD already claim
Make pending or unconfirmed balance policy explicit rather than implicit
Reduce silent stringly-typed state where narrow enums can enforce consistency

techStack.backendFramework: FastAPI with existing wallet verification service seams
techStack.frontend: Existing dashboard and wallet detail verification surfaces
techStack.testing: pytest service/API tests plus targeted browser smoke coverage
techStack.coreDependencies: Existing Bitcoin Core descriptor RPC flow, Electrum-compatible balance queries, and shipped Feature-23 verification persistence

userStories.title: Decimal-safe verified balance and drift arithmetic
acceptanceCriteria: Replace float-sensitive verified balance and drift calculations with Decimal-safe BTC arithmetic or a satoshi-first comparison model
Prevent false drift_detected or false verified outcomes caused by IEEE 754 rounding
Keep API payloads stable for web clients while tightening internal comparison semantics
userStories.testStrategy: pytest verification-service tests covering exact-match, tiny rounding edge cases, and drift thresholds

userStories.title: Real gap-limit-based discovery semantics
acceptanceCriteria: Make gap_limit materially affect address discovery rather than only storing it as metadata
Support iterative scanning or equivalent semantics that honor the declared discovery policy
Persist enough scan metadata to explain where and why a scan stopped
Keep operator ceilings and safety bounds in place so deep scans remain bounded
userStories.testStrategy: pytest verification-service tests with sparse/used-address fixtures and ceiling-hit scenarios

userStories.title: Confirmed versus unconfirmed balance policy
acceptanceCriteria: Define whether verification compares ledger balance to confirmed-only chain balance or to confirmed-plus-unconfirmed balance
If unconfirmed funds are considered, surface that fact explicitly in the recorded result and UI
Avoid a silent pass or drift outcome that hides pending funds semantics from the operator
userStories.testStrategy: pytest service and route tests for confirmed-only, pending-only, and mixed-balance scenarios

userStories.title: Verification-path performance cleanup
acceptanceCriteria: Reduce obvious repeated DB or table-initialization work on wallet and dashboard verification reads
Avoid redundant per-wallet verification lookups when building the portfolio dashboard
Preserve the shipped Electrum connection reuse improvements and extend cleanup only where it materially improves operator-facing responsiveness
userStories.testStrategy: pytest unit tests plus focused profiling or call-count assertions where practical

userStories.title: Typed verification status and coverage contracts
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the loosest verification status and coverage strings with typed enums or Literal-style constraints where practical
Keep route, persistence, and UI code aligned on one canonical set of verification state values
Avoid regressions in the shipped wallet and dashboard badge behavior
userStories.testStrategy: pytest model/API tests ensuring valid states serialize cleanly and invalid states are rejected

high: If gap-limit semantics remain weaker than the UI implies, operators may over-trust the Verified posture on deeper wallets
medium: Changing confirmed versus unconfirmed balance policy can shift operator-visible results and needs careful rollout language
Internal arithmetic and enum tightening can create subtle regressions if persistence and UI state handling drift out of sync
low: The architecture is already proven on real wallets; this phase is about hardening rather than proving viability

preFlightChecklist: Decide whether the verified balance contract is satoshi-first internally or Decimal-first with exact quantization at the boundaries
Define the exact stop condition for gap-limit discovery so the implementation and UI claim match
Lock the initial confirmed-versus-unconfirmed balance policy and operator wording before changing dashboard or wallet badge semantics
Identify the minimum dashboard and wallet-path query cleanup needed before adding more verification-derived surfaces
openQuestions: Should the default verification result compare against confirmed-only balance, with pending funds surfaced separately as operator context?
What exact iterative scan policy best matches the current first-run ceiling prompt while remaining understandable to operators?
